short: A philosopher-emperor whose reign was consumed by war and plague, and who broke with adoption to name his own son.
full:
Marcus Aurelius became emperor on 7 March 161 CE and immediately made his adoptive brother Lucius Verus co-emperor, the first time Rome had two emperors of equal rank. Where his predecessors had enjoyed peace, Marcus spent most of his reign on campaign, first against Parthia and then for over a decade against Germanic tribes along the Danube, while the empire absorbed a devastating plague brought back by returning soldiers.

He wrote his private philosophical reflections, the Meditations, largely in camp during these campaigns. In 177 CE he made his son Commodus co-emperor, ending the adoptive succession that had produced four capable rulers in a row and returning, for the first time in nearly a century, to a hereditary heir. Marcus died on campaign on 17 March 180 CE, leaving Commodus sole ruler at eighteen.
